content: Diethylpropion is a medication that works by suppressing appetite. It is prescribed for short-term use, typically a few weeks, and is combined with a calorie-restricted diet to assist with weight loss. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Diethylpropion is available in two forms: regular tablets and extended-release (long-acting) tablets. Regular tablets are usually taken three times daily, one hour before meals, while extended-release tablets are taken once daily, typically in the midmorning. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed. Do not crush, chew, or cut extended-release tablets; they must be swallowed whole. Be aware that diethylpropion has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take a larger dose, use it more frequently, or continue taking it for a longer duration than directed by your doctor. If you notice that the medication is no longer effective, contact your doctor. Before starting diethylpropion, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to diethylpropion, amphetamines, other weight-loss medications, or drugs used for allergies, hay fever, or colds. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, herbal products, and vitamins you are currently taking, especially guanethidine, insulin, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, even if you stopped taking them within the last two weeks. Let your doctor know if you have used other weight-loss medications in the past year. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking diethylpropion, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that diethylpropion may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this medication, so it is advisable to avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations while on diethylpropion. Typically, this involves adhering to a low-calorie, well-balanced diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Diethylpropion may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dry mouth, an unpleasant taste, restlessness, anxiety, dizziness, depression, tremors, upset stomach, vomiting, and increased urination. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include a fast or irregular heartbeat, heart palpitations, blurred vision, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing, chest pain, fainting, swelling of the ankles or feet, fever, sore throat, chills, and painful urination. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store diethylpropion in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor, as they may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Diethylpropion can affect blood sugar levels in diabetic patients and may mask some symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). If you notice changes in your blood or urine sugar test results, consult your doctor. Do not share this medication with others, and ask your pharmacist any questions you have about refilling your prescription. Diethylpropion is sold under the brand names Tenuate® and Tenuate Dospan®.
